item: The keyword scan hands the export each ranked keyword's language signature, so the export no longer re-reads the window's mention rows (C9 L1)
summary: fetch_signatures re-read the mention rows of every exported keyword to count its articles per language, which the ordered scan had already counted and thrown away. The ranker now carries that count for the rows it keeps (a one-language keyword derives it from the dominant language and its article count; only a keyword in several languages stores a flat tuple), and signatures_for rebuilds the dict, reading the mention rows only for a row that carried none. Priced in the memory plan as row units (SIG_BASE_BYTES 64 + SIG_PAIR_BYTES 48 per language, a bound on a measured tuple), so ROW_BYTES, HEAP_SHARE, SPILL_ROW_BYTES and memory_plan are unchanged; the spill table gains one column. MEASURED, cold (os.sync + posix_fadvise DONTNEED, fresh process, unperturbed) on 300,000 articles / 9,900,000 mentions, 3 runs each, alternating trees: 4096-page store 25.4-25.7 s before, 22.2-23.8 s after; 16384-page store 22.5-25.2 s before, 20.3-21.8 s after; the body is the same 2,104,960 bytes. Equality harness: 120 outputs (json, digest, zip x heap/spill x one/many batches x two windows) byte-identical to main, fetch_signatures called 0 times. Known effect, stated: the signature now comes from the scan's own snapshot, which is the export's snapshot; before it was a second read of the same read-only snapshot. The raw driver cursor (2.3-2.9 s more) is deliberately NOT used: it bypasses the three before_cursor_execute observers. The per-row loop body rewrite (L3) measured 0.2-0.6 s at 9.9 M rows, under the 1 s bar, and is not built.
